title: Traffic orchestration imbalance mitigation notes (Jun 2027)
content:
Purpose:
Short notes for the SRE/Release pairing to handle the observed traffic imbalances when shifting routing policies between capacity tiers. This is intentionally a pragmatic checklist + calendar + a rough release-notes draft to push to the docs repo after the run.

Context (summary):
- Over last month we saw uneven distribution across regions and model-variant buckets when the smart-router engaged cost-based throttling. Certain backend pools were saturated while others underutilized; client latencies spiked p95 in one region.
- Root cause appears to be mismatch between routing weight decay and autoscaler warmup for newly spun dedicated pods.
- Goal: reduce live user impact during upcoming policy change (priority-weighted->latency-first) and have clear rollback/fallback triggers.

Quick checklist (preflight, for day -3 -> day 0):
- [ ] Validate traffic shadowing pipeline works end-to-end (traffic-proxy v2) — Diego to run smoke shadow job (job id: shadow-2027-06-03).
- [ ] Confirm autoscaler warmup window increased to 120s in staging (SA config #73).
- [ ] Create synthetic burst tests mimicking 2x normal qps for top-10 customers (loadgen-cfg: ps-burst-2x).
- [ ] Verify prefix/KV cache priming is enabled for pinned models (cache-hit target >= 85%).
- [ ] Update routing policy to enable conservative weight shift: max 10% weight change per minute.
- [ ] Notify on-call SRE and product infra (channel #release-traffic) 24h and 1h prior.
- [ ] Hold manual rollback playbook in ready state (see section: rollback matrix).

Day-of quick ops run (Day 0):
- 09:00 — start controlled shift: 5% weight change every 10 min, observe p95 and error rate for 30 min windows.
- 09:30 — run canary traffic to new policy in region-us-west-2 (5% of total). Observe heap/backpressure signals.
- 10:00 — if p95 increase > 30% or 5xx > 0.5% above baseline — pause shift and revert last two minutes of weight changes.
- 11:00 — expand to 25% if no alerts; keep telemetry watch and manual throttle controls ready.

Telemetry gating (what to watch):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 per-route and aggregated — baseline vs live. Thresholds: p95 > baseline * 1.3 -> warning; p95 > baseline * 1.6 OR sustained p99 spike -> urgent.
- Errors: 5xx rate per-model > 0.5% absolute increase -> urgent.
- Queue depth and inflight limits: per-pool inflight > 75% of capacity for 2 consecutive minutes -> warning.
- Autoscaler churn: >3 scale events/min across cluster -> investigate.
- Cache churn: cache hit rate drop > 15% -> performance regression likely.

Smoke tests (post-change quick checks):
- Minimal prompts through hosted API for top 5 model variants (check token throughput and consistent KV cache behavior).
- Long-tail prompts to exercise attention/sequence lengths (check OOMs).
- Embedding requests at scale to ensure separate worker pools unaffected.

Rollback matrix (fast rollback steps):
- Level 1 (soft): Stop weight adjustments and revert to previous routing config (console -> routing -> revert). Time target: <3 min.
- Level 2 (medium): Trigger policy fallback to latency-first variant with region-fallback offload to dedicated pool v1. Time target: <10 min.
- Level 3 (hard): Revert the policy change commit in control-plane and resync routing engine (requires operator escalation). Time target: 20-30 min.

Communications plan (internal):
- 15-min cadence Slack updates in #release-traffic until stable or rollback. Use short status lines: OK/WARN/URGENT + top metric delta.
- Summary email to eng-leads and customer-success within 2 hours of final state.

Customer-facing notes (draft for release notes):
- Title: Routing policy update to improve latency stability and cost fairness
- Summary: We adjusted the smart-router weighting to prioritize lower-latency paths while preserving cost controls for non-latency-sensitive traffic. The change will reduce tail latency for interactive workloads. A small fraction of heavy-batched requests may experience transient reroutes during the rollout window.
- Impact: No planned downtime. Performance expectation — typical p95 latency should improve for interactive routes; batched jobs might see slight increases during rebalancing windows.
- Action for customers: None required. If you see sustained errors, open a ticket with support referencing INCIDENT-ROUTER-2027-06.

Open questions and TODOs:
- Do we have an updated weight-decay model tested under synthetic multi-tenant scenarios? (need: bench run with 50 tenants).
- Should we pre-warm dedicated pools for top-10 customers rather than rely on autoscaler alone? (cost trade-offs).
- Evaluate whether TTL on KV cache evictions should be extended from 30m -> 90m for pinned models.
- Confirm observability retention settings for the next 72h (higher retention window during rollout recommended).

Post-roll postmortem skeleton (notes to self):
- Capture timeline (minute granularity) of weight changes + alerts triggered.
- Cross-reference with autoscaler logs and instance creation latency.
- Customer-impact assessment: query support tickets for related errors in window.
- Cost delta: measure token-unit cost for 72h pre/post.

Short mental checklist for the operator (cheat-sheet):
- Before touching weights: notify -> snapshot current routing state -> run preflight tests.
- Small increments only, observe for at least 10-15 minutes between steps.
- If multiple teams are making changes, lock the routing UI and coordinate via #release-traffic.

Appendix (links and quick commands):
- PR to watch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/987
- Jira: RELEASE-1345 (policy-change), AUTOSCALE-662 (warmup change)
- Quick console commands: 
  - fetch routing snapshot: rctl routing snapshot --out /tmp/route-snap.json
  - revert last config: rctl routing revert --last

Notes to self (rough, unpolished):
- We should consider a small canary that shifts only a surrogate-weight (mirror mode) before touching live weights — harder to build but safer.
- Diego: double-check the loadgen scenarios include edge-case token lengths; last run missed the 16k token scenario.
- Priya: can you run an experiment on whether 90s autoscaler warmup materially changes pod churn?

End.
__notes: internal: sketch, will iterate. keep in shared drive until postmortem finalized
